sentenceSets.sentence: She had arrived at the position by her own volition, which made her less inclined to accept the framing that she had been installed.

answerChoices.reasoning: She may have been chosen based on merit, but 'merit' describes worthiness; the sentence emphasizes her own choice and determination.
'Choice' describes picking an option; the sentence emphasizes her will and determination to decide, not merely selecting among options.
'Decision' describes the act of choosing; the sentence emphasizes her power of will and self-determination.
'Determination' describes firmness of resolve; the sentence emphasizes her power of will and choice specifically.
She may have worked hard to achieve the position, but 'effort' emphasizes the work done; the sentence shows her own power of will and choice.
She may have been ambitious, but 'ambition' emphasizes desire and aspiration; the sentence shows her power of will to act.
'Initiative' describes taking action on one's own; the sentence emphasizes her power of will and choosing, not just taking action.
'Agency' describes capacity to act; the sentence emphasizes her power of will and choosing specifically.
She arrived at the position by her own will and choice, the opposite of being selected by luck or circumstance that 'chance' implies.
She deliberately chose to pursue the position through her own will; 'accident' means an unplanned event, the opposite of volition.
She arrived by her own power of will and choosing; 'fate' means predetermined events beyond one's control, opposite to volition.

sentenceSets.sentence: Though the parents pressured him to study medicine, he pursued architecture by his own volition, insisting that his life direction had to be his own.

answerChoices.reasoning: He may be rebelling against parental pressure, but 'rebellion' emphasizes opposition; the sentence shows his own power of will and self-determination.
'Preference' describes liking one thing over another; the sentence shows his power of will and self-determined choice, not merely preference.
'Desire' describes wanting something; the sentence emphasizes his power of will and determination to choose his own path.
'Choice' describes selecting an option; the sentence emphasizes his power of will and self-determination, insisting on autonomy.
He is interested in architecture, but 'interest' describes attraction; the sentence emphasizes his power of will to determine his own path.
'Will' is near synonymous with volition; the sentence specifically emphasizes volition as his exercising independent determination.
He is convinced that his path must be his own, but 'conviction' emphasizes strong belief; the sentence shows his power of will.
'Independence' describes self-reliance; the sentence emphasizes his power of will and choosing, not independence in general.
He pursues his own chosen path against parental pressure; 'obligation' means duty or necessity, opposite to his self-determined volition.
He pursues architecture by his own power of will despite parental pressure; 'coercion' means forced compliance, opposite to volition.
He insists that his life direction must be his own will; 'compulsion' describes an irresistible force, opposite to freely exercised volition.

sentenceSets.sentence: The employees transferred to the new office by their own volition, understanding that the relocation offered better opportunities despite the inconvenience.

answerChoices.reasoning: 'Consent' means agreeing or permitting; the employees consent, but the sentence emphasizes their power of will and self-determination.
'Agreement' describes mutual assent; the employees agree, but the sentence emphasizes their own power of will and choosing.
'Acceptance' describes receiving or assenting to something; the sentence emphasizes their power of will and self-determined choice.
'Permission' describes being allowed to do something; the sentence emphasizes their power of will and self-determination, not needing permission.
They may have received approval, but 'approval' emphasizes getting permission; the sentence shows their own power of will and choice.
They make a decision, but 'decision' emphasizes the act of choosing; the sentence emphasizes their power of will and self-determination.
'Willingness' describes being ready to do something; the sentence emphasizes their power of will and self-determined choosing specifically.
They may be enthusiastic about opportunities, but 'enthusiasm' emphasizes emotional intensity; the sentence shows their power of will.
The employees transfer by their own power of will and choice; 'compulsion' means an irresistible force, opposite to volition.
They transfer by their own will and determination; 'mandate' means an authoritative order, opposite to their self-determined volition.
They choose to transfer by their own will; 'requirement' means something necessary or demanded, opposite to self-determined volition.
